When no worker count is declared, a new cluster autoscales from 1 to 8 workers and an existing one keeps its shape. Ignored when singleNode is true.
PyPI packages installed on the cluster, as pip requirement strings, e.g. pandas==2.2.2. Installed only when the agent creates the cluster; later changes are not applied to an existing cluster.

Azure region the resource is created in, as an Azure location name (e.g. 'westeurope'). When unset, the region of the Live System's resource group, which is the Live System's own region parameter, else the environment agent's region, else the region the agent is deployed in; with none of these, creating the group is refused until one is set on the environment's Azure agent or here. An existing resource stays where it is deployed. The legacy key 'azureRegion' is still read when 'region' is blank.
When true, the cluster runs a driver only, with Spark in local mode, whatever the worker counts say; the agent adds the single-node Spark settings and tags Databricks requires. When unset, false.

User or service principal a single-user (dedicated) cluster is assigned to; used only when dataSecurityMode is SINGLE_USER, DATA_SECURITY_MODE_DEDICATED, LEGACY_SINGLE_USER or LEGACY_SINGLE_USER_STANDARD. When unset, the existing cluster's assignee, else the principal the agent authenticates to the workspace as; if neither is found the cluster is created without one.

Spark configuration of the cluster as key/value pairs, e.g. spark.sql.shuffle.partitions. The agent adds the single-node settings and the settings of linked Event Hubs, then edits the cluster whenever its Spark configuration differs from the result, so keys set outside the blueprint are removed.

derived.note: an existing cluster's own runtime, else the newest general-purpose LTS runtime the workspace offers

params.description: Databricks Runtime version key, e.g. 15.4.x-scala2.12. A declared value is used verbatim and a change edits (restarts) the running cluster. When unset, an existing cluster keeps the runtime it runs; a new cluster gets the newest general-purpose LTS runtime the workspace offers, and the component fails if none is found.

rules.message: A PYTHON job needs the Python file it runs.

rules.fix: Set taskType (NOTEBOOK, PYTHON or SPARK_JAR) together with the artifact it runs, or set artifactUri and entryPoint for a Python wheel job.
rules.message: The job does not say what to run.

params.description: Kind of artifact named by artifactUri: python_wheel runs it as a Python wheel task, notebook runs the job by taskType and its artifact key instead. When unset, a job with an artifactUri is a Python wheel job.

http(s) URL of the Python wheel the job runs; the agent downloads it and uploads it to the workspace on every reconcile. Setting it makes the job a Python wheel job unless artifactType says otherwise, and then entryPoint is required. Only http(s) URLs are supported: any other value, a bare reference or an oci:// URI included, fails the job naming artifactUri.
Quartz cron expression the job runs on, evaluated in UTC (seconds first: '0 0 2 * * ?' is 02:00 every day). When unset, the job has no schedule and runs only when triggered.
the function the wheel exposes
Arguments passed to entryPoint of a Python wheel job, as a list of strings in order. When unset, none.

deprecated.note: the job runs on the cluster it depends on, or on a cluster started for each run when it depends on none

params.description: Legacy flag, ignored: the job runs on the cluster it depends on, or on a new cluster started for each run when it depends on none. A value contradicting that placement is reported as a warning; the placement applied is published as the clusterPlacement output.

URI of the JAR that holds mainClassName, installed as the library of a SPARK_JAR job's task (a workspace path, a /Volumes path, or a cloud-storage URI the workspace can read). When unset, the JAR must already be on the cluster. Refused on a job that is not a SPARK_JAR job.

derived.note: defaults to the component id

params.description: Name of the job in the Databricks workspace; the agent finds its job by this name on every reconcile, so renaming it creates a new job. When unset, the component id.
Fully qualified main class a SPARK_JAR job runs; 'parameters' are passed to its main method. The JAR holding it must already be available on the cluster.
How many times Databricks retries a failed run of the task. When unset or 0, a failed run is not retried.

params.description: Databricks node type of the per-run cluster's driver and workers, as listed by the workspace. When unset, an existing job keeps the node type it runs on; a new one gets the newest-generation, smallest general-purpose node type of at least 4 cores the workspace offers and the account has capacity for, and is refused when none is found.
the workspace path of the notebook the job runs

params.description: Python package name inside the wheel, used by a Python wheel job. When unset, the component id.

Arguments for the task, as a list of strings. A PYTHON or SPARK_JAR job receives them as command-line arguments in order; a NOTEBOOK job receives the entries written key=value as notebook parameters and ignores the rest. Not used by a Python wheel job, which reads entryPointArgs.
the path of the Python file the job runs

Azure region the resource is created in, as an Azure location name (e.g. 'westeurope'). An existing resource stays where it is deployed. The legacy key 'azureRegion' is still read when 'region' is blank.

params.description: Which artifact Databricks executes: NOTEBOOK (notebookPath), PYTHON (pythonFile) or SPARK_JAR (mainClassName), matched without regard to case. When unset, derived only when exactly one of those three keys is set; with none or several set the job is refused. Ignored for a Python wheel job (artifactUri / artifactType python_wheel).

URI where MLflow stores the experiment's artifacts, e.g. a dbfs:/ or abfss:// path. When unset, the workspace's default artifact store. Immutable after creation: a different value on an existing experiment fails the component.

MLflow experiment name, an absolute workspace path such as /Shared/churn-model; a name without a leading / is placed under /Shared/. When unset or blank, /Shared/<component id>. An existing experiment of that name is adopted.

Azure region the resource is created in, as an Azure location name (e.g. 'westeurope'). When unset, the region of the Live System's resource group, which is the Live System's own region parameter, else the environment agent's region, else the region the agent is deployed in; with none of these, creating the group is refused until one is set on the environment's Azure agent or here. An existing resource stays where it is deployed. The legacy key 'azureRegion' is still read when 'region' is blank.
Default blob access tier: Hot, Cool, Cold or Premium. When unset, Hot. Ignored for kind Storage and BlockBlobStorage, which have no account-level tier.
Whether containers of this account may allow anonymous public read access. When unset, false.
Whether object replication to accounts in another Microsoft Entra tenant is allowed. When unset, false.
Whether requests may authorize with the account access key (Shared Key, including account SAS). When unset, true. Set false to allow only Microsoft Entra ID authorization.

Restricts copy operations to and from the account: PrivateLink (same virtual network via private link) or AAD (same Microsoft Entra tenant). When unset, copies are not restricted. A value outside the two is sent to Azure with a warning; a catalog placeholder is refused.

Identity-based authentication for Azure Files, as {directoryServiceOptions, defaultSharePermission, activeDirectoryProperties}. directoryServiceOptions is None, AADDS, AD or AADKERB and defaultSharePermission a share-level role name, both None when not named; activeDirectoryProperties carries the on-premises AD domain facts (domainName, domainGuid, domainSid, forestName, netBiosDomainName, azureStorageSid, samAccountName, accountType, default Computer) needed for AD. When unset, none is configured.

Legacy alias of region: the Azure region a new storage account is created in, e.g. northeurope. region wins when both are set. When both are unset, the region of the component's resource group, which is the Live System's (environment's) region; a new account with no region at all is refused. An existing account keeps the region it lives in: Azure cannot move it.

Azure Backup for the account's file shares, as {vaultName, vaultResourceGroupName, vaultLocation, sku, etag, policyName, policyResourceGroupName, policyLocation, policy, policyType}. Defaults: vault <account>-backupVault and policy <account>-policy, both in the account's resource group and region, vault SKU Standard, policyType AzureStorage. policy is the policy JSON; when empty, only the vault is created. When unset, no backup is configured.
Custom domain for the blob endpoint, as {name, useSubDomainName}. A block without a name means no custom domain; on an existing account an unset value keeps the domain it has.
Whether the Azure portal authorizes with Microsoft Entra ID by default instead of the account key. When unset, false.
Endpoint DNS type: Standard or AzureDnsZone (partitioned DNS zones, allowing many more accounts per subscription). When unset, Standard. Fixed when the account is created.

Encryption at rest, as {keySource, keyVaultProperties: {keyName, keyVaultUri, keyVersion}, identity: {userAssignedIdentity, federatedIdentityClientId}, requireInfrastructureEncryption, services: {blob|file|queue|table: {enabled, keyType}}}. keySource is Microsoft.Storage (default) or Microsoft.Keyvault for customer-managed keys. When unset, Microsoft-managed keys with blob and file encryption enabled.

Azure Edge Zone to place the account in, as {name, type}; type defaults to EdgeZone. A block without a name means no extended location. On an existing account an unset value keeps what the account has.

File service soft delete, as {deleteRetentionEnabled, deleteRetentionDays}. Applied only for kind Storage or FileStorage. When neither field is named, the file service is left untouched; a named policy without days writes 0 days.

Managed identity of the account, as {type, userAssignedIdentities}: type is None, SystemAssigned, UserAssigned or 'SystemAssigned,UserAssigned' (None when the block has no type); userAssignedIdentities maps user-assigned identity resource IDs to empty objects. When unset, the account gets no managed identity.

Account-level version immutability (WORM), as {enabled, immutabilityPolicy: {immutabilityPeriodSinceCreationInDays, state: Disabled|Unlocked|Locked, allowProtectedAppendWrites}}. Only the fields named are applied; the rest keep the account's own values. A Locked policy cannot be undone.

Whether the hierarchical namespace (Data Lake Storage Gen2) is enabled. Set at creation only. When unset, a new account is created with it, as an ADLS Gen2 data lake requires; an existing account keeps the namespace it was created with.
Whether local users (used by SFTP) are enabled. When unset, Azure's default applies.
Whether NFS 3.0 is enabled for blobs. Set at creation only and requires the hierarchical namespace (isHnsEnabled). When unset, it is not enabled.
Whether the SFTP endpoint is enabled. Requires the hierarchical namespace (isHnsEnabled). When unset, it is not enabled.

Access-key expiration policy, as {keyExpirationPeriodInDays}, at least 1 day. A block without a period keeps an existing account's period and gives a new account 30 days. When unset, no key policy is requested.

Storage account kind: StorageV2, Storage, BlobStorage, BlockBlobStorage or FileStorage. When unset, StorageV2. It also picks the defaults of sku and accessTier, and whether fileService applies (only Storage and FileStorage).
Large file shares (up to 100 TiB): Enabled or Disabled. Once enabled it cannot be disabled. When unset, it is not requested. A catalog placeholder is refused.
Minimum TLS version accepted by the account: TLS1_0, TLS1_1 or TLS1_2. When unset, TLS1_2.

Network firewall of the account, as {defaultAction: Allow|Deny, bypass, ipRules: [{ipAddressOrRange, action}], virtualNetworkRules: [{virtualNetworkResourceId, action, state}], resourceAccessRules: [{resourceId, tenantId}]}. Every listed rule field is required. defaultAction defaults from publicAccess; bypass (e.g. AzureServices, Logging, Metrics) and rule lists not named keep what an existing account has. When unset, only the defaultAction derived from publicAccess.
Default network action when networkRuleSet names none: true is Allow, false is Deny, so only bypassed Azure services and listed rules reach the account. When unset, false (Deny).
Whether the public endpoint is reachable at all: Enabled or Disabled. When unset, Enabled; what reaches it is then decided by the network rule set (see publicAccess).

Azure region the resource is created in, as an Azure location name (e.g. 'westeurope'). When unset, the region of the Live System's resource group, which is the Live System's own region parameter, else the environment agent's region, else the region the agent is deployed in; with none of these, creating the group is refused until one is set on the environment's Azure agent or here. An existing resource stays where it is deployed. The legacy key 'azureRegion' is still read when 'region' is blank.

Network routing preference, as {routingChoice: MicrosoftRouting|InternetRouting (default InternetRouting), publishMicrosoftEndpoints (default false), publishInternetEndpoints (default true)}. When unset, none is requested.

Shared access signature expiration policy, as {sasExpirationPeriod, expirationAction}. The period has the form <days>.<hours>:<minutes>:<seconds>, e.g. 1.00:00:00; the action is Log or Block. A field not named keeps the account's own value; on a new account a missing period is one day and a missing action Log. When unset, no SAS policy is requested.
Storage SKU (redundancy and performance), e.g. Standard_LRS, Standard_ZRS, Standard_GRS or Premium_LRS. When unset, Premium_LRS for kind BlockBlobStorage and Standard_LRS otherwise.
Whether the account accepts HTTPS only. When unset, true.

Reference to a secret defined on the environment, written {"$envSecret": "<shortName>"}. The environment owns the value: the component only resolves and publishes it, and deleting the component leaves the secret in place. Preferred over 'secretValue'; when both are set, this one wins. Fails when no environment secret has that short name.

Name under which 'secretValue' is stored in the environment secret store. When unset, the component id. Ignored when 'secret' references an environment secret, which keeps its own name. Changing it writes a new secret and revokes the readers' grants on the old one.

Raw secret value (legacy) that the component stores in the environment secret store under 'secretName', granting read access to the custom workloads linked to it. Required when 'secret' is not set; deleting the component deletes the stored secret.

App Service plan the app runs on: {name? (asp-default), pricingPlan? (e.g. BASIC_B1, STANDARD_S1, PREMIUM_P1V3, as a string or {name}), numberOfWorkers? (1), operatingSystem? (Linux; any other value is Windows), zoneRedundancyEnabled? (false), azureRegion? (the app's region), azureResourceGroup? ({name, region}), tags?}. When unset, plan asp-default, BASIC_B1 with 1 worker, Linux, in the Live System's resource group and the app's region (its region, else its resource group's). A container-image function needs a Linux plan. An existing app keeps the plan it is bound to; a plan can be shared by several apps.

Application settings as a name to value map, added to the settings the agent sets itself (AzureWebJobsStorage, FUNCTIONS_EXTENSION_VERSION, FUNCTIONS_WORKER_RUNTIME and the package settings). A declared name replaces the agent's setting of that name, compared without regard to case, so FUNCTIONS_WORKER_RUNTIME can be chosen here. A change alone is not detected as drift on an existing app.

Site configuration: {applicationStack?: {nodeVersion | pythonVersion | dotnetVersion | javaVersion | powerShellVersion}, alwaysOn? (true), http2Enabled? (true), minimumTlsVersion? (1.2), ftpsState? (Disabled), healthCheckPath?, corsSettings?: {allowedOrigins, supportCredentials?}}. The first applicationStack version set picks the runtime; when none is, Node 20. dotnetVersion runs the .NET isolated worker (FUNCTIONS_WORKER_RUNTIME dotnet-isolated): the in-process model is retired (.NET 8, the last version offering it, leaves support on 2026-11-10). A deployed app running the in-process worker keeps it, with a contract warning; appSettings.FUNCTIONS_WORKER_RUNTIME chooses explicitly. On an existing app, only a runtime stack change is detected as drift.

Managed identity of the app as {type}, type an Azure managed identity type such as 'SystemAssigned' or 'None'. When unset, SystemAssigned, which a container-image function uses to pull from the registry. The identity's principal ID is published as the principalId output.
Overrides how sourceArtifact is classified: 'image' or 'zip'. When unset, detected from the artifact's manifest. 'zip' on an artifact that is a container image fails the component.

Azure region the resource is created in, as an Azure location name (e.g. 'westeurope'). When unset, the region of the Live System's resource group, which is the Live System's own region parameter, else the environment agent's region, else the region the agent is deployed in; with none of these, creating the group is refused until one is set on the environment's Azure agent or here. An existing resource stays where it is deployed. The legacy key 'azureRegion' is still read when 'region' is blank.

OCI artifact holding the function code, as '<registry>/<repository>:<tag>': in an Azure Container Registry, read with the agent's managed identity and pulled with the app's, or in a registry serving anonymous pulls. A container image is run as a Linux container function; a zip is staged to a blob and run from package. Redeployed only when the artifact's digest changes. When unset, the app is created with its runtime stack and no code.

Connection string of the storage account the Functions host uses (AzureWebJobsStorage). Required for a zip sourceArtifact, which is staged to a blob in that account: such a component fails without it.

Azure region the resource is created in, as an Azure location name (e.g. 'westeurope'). When unset, the region of the Live System's resource group, which is the Live System's own region parameter, else the environment agent's region, else the region the agent is deployed in; with none of these, creating the group is refused until one is set on the environment's Azure agent or here. An existing resource stays where it is deployed. The legacy key 'azureRegion' is still read when 'region' is blank.
CPU cores for the container (e.g. 0.25, 0.5, 1). When unset, 0.5. Must be a combination with memory that Azure Container Apps accepts.
When true, the app is published on a public FQDN with no authentication in front of it. When unset, false: ingress is internal to the Container Apps environment.
Container image reference to run, e.g. 'registry/repository:tag'. Required to create: a deployed one declared without it keeps the image it runs. A change is applied as a new revision.
Legacy spelling of 'region', read only when 'region' is blank.
Maximum number of replicas. When unset, 10.
Memory for the container as an Azure quantity string, e.g. '1Gi' or '0.5Gi'. When unset, 1Gi. Must match the cpu value per Azure Container Apps' allowed combinations.
Minimum number of replicas. When unset, 0: the app scales to zero when idle.
Port the container listens on; the ingress target port. When unset, 8080.
Azure location the app is created in (e.g. 'westeurope'). When unset, 'location', else the legacy 'azureRegion', else the region of the Live System's resource group. Applied when the app is created.
CPU cores requested for the container (fractions allowed). When unset, 1. Changing it deletes and recreates the container group.
DNS label for the public IP, giving the FQDN '<label>.<region>.azurecontainer.io'. Used only when publicIp is true. Applied when the container group is created.

Container image reference to run, e.g. 'registry/repository:tag'. Required to create: a deployed one declared without it keeps the image it runs. Changing it deletes and recreates the container group.

Azure location the container group is created in (e.g. 'westeurope'). When unset, the component's region: 'region', else the legacy 'azureRegion', else its resource group's region. Applied when the container group is created.
Memory requested for the container, in GB. When unset, 1.5. Changing it deletes and recreates the container group.
TCP port the container listens on and the group exposes. When unset, 8080. Applied when the container group is created.
When true, the container group gets a public IP address; otherwise a private one. Applied when the container group is created.

Azure region the resource is created in, as an Azure location name (e.g. 'westeurope'). When unset, the region of the Live System's resource group, which is the Live System's own region parameter, else the environment agent's region, else the region the agent is deployed in; with none of these, creating the group is refused until one is set on the environment's Azure agent or here. An existing resource stays where it is deployed. The legacy key 'azureRegion' is still read when 'region' is blank.
Container group restart policy: Always, OnFailure or Never (case-sensitive). Any other value means Always. Applied when the container group is created.

App Service plan the app runs on: {name? (asp-default), pricingPlan? (e.g. BASIC_B1, STANDARD_S1, PREMIUM_P1V3, as a string or {name}), numberOfWorkers? (1), operatingSystem? (Linux; any other value is Windows), zoneRedundancyEnabled? (false), azureRegion? (the app's region), azureResourceGroup? ({name, region}), tags?}. When unset, plan asp-default, BASIC_B1 with 1 worker, Linux, in the Live System's resource group and the app's region (its region, else its resource group's). An existing app keeps the plan it is bound to.

Legacy alias of region: the region a new App Service plan is created in when appServicePlan declares no azureRegion. When unset, region, else the resource group's region. A web app always runs in its plan's region (Azure refuses any other), and an existing plan never moves.
the git branch the workload deploys from

Key Vault certificates for the custom domains: [{keyVaultId, name, passwordSecretId?, region?, tags?}], keyVaultId the vault's ARM ID, name the Key Vault secret holding the certificate, passwordSecretId an environment secret with the PFX password (empty password when unset). Imported into the app's resource group; certificates no longer listed are removed.
Short name of the environment's CI/CD profile for the workload. Read and not used by this offer.
When true, ARR affinity cookies keep a client on one instance. When unset, Azure's default. Applied when the web app is created; later changes are not applied to an existing app.

When true, the app asks clients for a TLS certificate, as set by clientCertMode. When unset, Azure's default (off). Applied when the web app is created; later changes are not applied to an existing app.
Comma-separated request paths exempt from client certificate authentication. Applied when the web app is created; later changes are not applied to an existing app.

Client certificate mode when clientCertEnabled is true: Required, Optional or OptionalInteractiveUser. When unset, Azure's default. Applied when the web app is created; later changes are not applied to an existing app.

Creates the app as a clone of another: Azure cloningInfo {sourceWebAppId, sourceWebAppLocation?, overwrite?, cloneCustomHostNames?, cloneSourceControl?, appSettingsOverrides?, hostingEnvironment?, configureLoadBalancing?, trafficManagerProfileId?, trafficManagerProfileName?, correlationId?}. Used only when the web app is created.

Site configuration as a map of Azure siteConfig properties, e.g. appSettings (name to value map), connectionStrings, alwaysOn (true), http20Enabled (true), ftpsState (Disabled), minTlsVersion (1.2), healthCheckPath, corsSettings, ipSecurityRestrictions, linuxFxVersion. Applied when the web app is created; later changes are not applied to an existing app.
Size of the function container, in MB (Azure siteConfig containerSize). When unset, Azure's default. Applied when the web app is created; later changes are not applied to an existing app.
Identifier Azure uses to verify the custom domains assigned to the app (the asuid TXT record value). Applied when the web app is created; later changes are not applied to an existing app.
Host names bound to the web app with SNI TLS, using the certificates. Bindings of host names no longer listed are deleted; the default azurewebsites.net host name is never touched.
Daily memory-time quota in GB-seconds, for apps on a dynamic (consumption) plan; 0 means no quota. Applied when the web app is created; later changes are not applied to an existing app.
Whether the site is enabled; false creates it stopped. When unset, the site is enabled (Azure's default). Applied when the web app is created; later changes are not applied to an existing app.

When true, the app's public host names are disabled and it is reachable only through API Management. When unset, Azure's default (false). Applied when the web app is created; later changes are not applied to an existing app.
ARM resource ID of the App Service Environment that hosts the app. When unset, the multi-tenant service. Applied when the web app is created; later changes are not applied to an existing app.
When true, plain HTTP requests are redirected to HTTPS. When unset, true. Applied when the web app is created; later changes are not applied to an existing app.
When true, the app runs in a Hyper-V sandbox (Windows containers). When unset, Azure's default (false). Applied when the web app is created; later changes are not applied to an existing app.
Secret holding the passphrase of the private SSH deploy key. Read and not used by this offer.
Secret holding the private SSH deploy key of the repository. Read and not used by this offer.
Publishing user name of the site configuration. When unset, Azure's default. Applied when the web app is created; later changes are not applied to an existing app.
Site redundancy mode: None, Manual, Failover, ActiveActive or GeoRedundant. When unset, Azure's default. Applied when the web app is created; later changes are not applied to an existing app.

Azure region the resource is created in, as an Azure location name (e.g. 'westeurope'). When unset, the region of the Live System's resource group, which is the Live System's own region parameter, else the environment agent's region, else the region the agent is deployed in; with none of these, creating the group is refused until one is set on the environment's Azure agent or here. the full name (owner/name) of the git repository the workload deploys from

Azure's reserved flag: true for a Linux app. The plan's operating system is set by appServicePlan.operatingSystem. When unset, Azure's default. Applied when the web app is created; later changes are not applied to an existing app.

Azure roles granted to the app's user-assigned managed identity: [{name, scope, roleType?}], name a role name, scope an ARM resource ID, roleType BuiltInRole when unset. Ocelot roles are skipped. Assigned on every reconcile.
When true, the SCM (Kudu) site is stopped together with the app. When unset, Azure's default (false). Applied when the web app is created; later changes are not applied to an existing app.
the SSH URI of the git repository the workload deploys from
When true, the app requires a customer-provided storage account. When unset, Azure's default (false). Applied when the web app is created; later changes are not applied to an existing app.

ARM resource ID of the subnet the app joins for regional VNet integration (/subscriptions/.../virtualNetworks/<vnet>/subnets/<subnet>). When unset, no VNet integration. Applied when the web app is created; later changes are not applied to an existing app.
Name of the secret holding the workload's service-mesh client ID. Read and not used by this offer.
Name of the secret holding the workload's service-mesh client secret. Read and not used by this offer.

Fails when no environment secret has that short name.

Kafka ACLs of the user, which authenticates with a TLS client certificate and is named after the component id. Outbound rules: [{protocol?, fromPort?, toPort?, sourceCidr | destCidr | sourceComponentId}]; the CIDR or component is the destination. An omitted toPort means the single port fromPort. Unset leaves the group's egress untouched; declared (even empty) the rules are exactly these. On Azure each rule is an outbound allow; the NSG's built-in AllowInternetOutBound still applies below them. A rule whose destination is a component is skipped: Azure cannot match an NSG without an Application Security Group.

Inbound allow rules: [{protocol?, fromPort?, toPort?, sourceCidr | sourceComponentId}]. protocol defaults to tcp; an omitted toPort means the single port fromPort, and a rule with no fromPort covers all ports. An entry with neither source is skipped, and a rule whose source is a component is skipped (Azure cannot match an NSG without an Application Security Group). When non-empty, the agent's inbound rules are made exactly these; unset or empty leaves the NSG's inbound rules untouched.

Whether the Azure portal authorizes with Microsoft Entra ID by default instead of the account key. When unset, false.
Endpoint DNS type: Standard or AzureDnsZone (partitioned DNS zones, allowing many more accounts per subscription). When unset, Standard. Fixed when the account is created.

Encryption at rest, as {keySource, keyVaultProperties: {keyName, keyVaultUri, keyVersion}, identity: {userAssignedIdentity, federatedIdentityClientId}, requireInfrastructureEncryption, services: {blob|file|queue|table: {enabled, keyType}}}. keySource is Microsoft.Storage (default) or Microsoft.Keyvault for customer-managed keys. When unset, Microsoft-managed keys with blob and file encryption enabled.

Azure Edge Zone to place the account in, as {name, type}; type defaults to EdgeZone. A block without a name means no extended location. On an existing account an unset value keeps what the account has.

Managed identity of the account, as {type, userAssignedIdentities}: type is None, SystemAssigned, UserAssigned or 'SystemAssigned,UserAssigned' (None when the block has no type); userAssignedIdentities maps user-assigned identity resource IDs to empty objects. When unset, the account gets no managed identity.

Account-level version immutability (WORM), as {enabled, immutabilityPolicy: {immutabilityPeriodSinceCreationInDays, state: Disabled|Unlocked|Locked, allowProtectedAppendWrites}}. Only the fields named are applied; the rest keep the account's own values. A Locked policy cannot be undone.

Whether the hierarchical namespace (Data Lake Storage Gen2) is enabled. Set at creation only. When unset, a new account is created without it and an existing account keeps the namespace it was created with.
Whether local users (used by SFTP) are enabled. When unset, Azure's default applies.
Whether NFS 3.0 is enabled for blobs. Set at creation only and requires the hierarchical namespace (isHnsEnabled). When unset, it is not enabled.
Whether the SFTP endpoint is enabled. Requires the hierarchical namespace (isHnsEnabled). When unset, it is not enabled.

Storage account kind: StorageV2, Storage, BlobStorage, BlockBlobStorage or FileStorage. When unset, StorageV2. It also picks the defaults of sku and accessTier, and whether fileService applies (only Storage and FileStorage).
Large file shares (up to 100 TiB): Enabled or Disabled. Once enabled it cannot be disabled. When unset, it is not requested. A catalog placeholder is refused.
Minimum TLS version accepted by the account: TLS1_0, TLS1_1 or TLS1_2. When unset, TLS1_2.

Network firewall of the account, as {defaultAction: Allow|Deny, bypass, ipRules: [{ipAddressOrRange, action}], virtualNetworkRules: [{virtualNetworkResourceId, action, state}], resourceAccessRules: [{resourceId, tenantId}]}. When unset, only the defaultAction derived from publicAccess.
Default network action when networkRuleSet names none: true is Allow, false is Deny, so only bypassed Azure services and listed rules reach the account. When unset, false (Deny).

Network routing preference, as {routingChoice: MicrosoftRouting|InternetRouting (default InternetRouting), publishMicrosoftEndpoints (default false), publishInternetEndpoints (default true)}. When unset, none is requested.

Whether the account accepts HTTPS only. When unset, true.

Whether writes are forced to use defaultEncryptionScope, refusing a per-blob scope. When unset, false.

Container-level version immutability (WORM), as {enabled}. Sent only when enabled is named; the storage account must support version-level immutability. When unset, nothing is requested.
Container metadata as name-value string pairs. When unset or empty, no metadata is sent.
Anonymous read access: None, Blob (blobs only) or Container (blobs and listing). When unset, None. Anything but None also needs allowBlobPublicAccess on the storage account.

Azure region the resource is created in, as an Azure location name (e.g. 'westeurope'). An existing resource stays where it is deployed. The legacy key 'azureRegion' is still read when 'region' is blank.

Reference to a secret defined on the environment, written {"$envSecret": "<shortName>"}. The environment owns the value: the component only resolves and publishes it, and deleting the component leaves the secret in place. Preferred over 'secretValue'; when both are set, this one wins. Fails when no environment secret has that short name.

Name under which 'secretValue' is stored in the environment secret store. When unset, the component id. Ignored when 'secret' references an environment secret, which keeps its own name. Changing it writes a new secret and revokes the readers' grants on the old one.

Raw secret value (legacy) that the component stores in the environment secret store under 'secretName', granting read access to the custom workloads linked to it. Required when 'secret' is not set; deleting the component deletes the stored secret.
